# How to Access ESPN's Hidden API for Free Sports Data

Discover how to access ESPN’s hidden API and pull live sports data for free with simple GET requests.

![Adrian Horning](https://thewebscrapingguy.com/me.png)

by Adrian Horning

Aug 26, 2025

Copy link

![Treasure chest with ESPN logo spilling JSON labeled Stats, Scores, and API endpoints.](https://scrapecreators.com/_astro/featured.9t5jkv9E_NXkKi.png)

The **ESPN API** is the JSON backend ESPN.com uses to load scores, stats, and game summaries. You can call it with simple GET requests— **no API key required**.

That opens up real jobs for developers:

- Pull **box scores**, play-by-play, and rosters for NBA and NFL games
- Find game IDs from ESPN URLs and swap them into endpoint templates
- Build dashboards and fantasy tools _without a paid sports data contract_

Most sports APIs charge for keys or cap free tiers. ESPN’s **site.web.api.espn.com** endpoints are one of the fastest ways to experiment with structured sports data.

**In this guide, you’ll learn:**

- [Where ESPN’s API lives and how to spot calls in your browser](https://scrapecreators.com/blog/espn-api-sports-data#where-the-espn-api-lives)
- [A real walkthrough using 2016 NBA Finals Game 7](https://scrapecreators.com/blog/espn-api-sports-data#real-example-2016-nba-finals-game-7)
- [What data a single game summary returns](https://scrapecreators.com/blog/espn-api-sports-data#the-full-espn-api-endpoint)
- [How to explore other sports and event IDs](https://scrapecreators.com/blog/espn-api-sports-data#how-to-explore-more-data)

Here’s the endpoint walkthrough.

## Where the ESPN API Lives

ESPN’s site makes API calls to:

[https://site.web.api.espn.com/apis](https://site.web.api.espn.com/apis)

This endpoint is wide open. You don’t need authentication keys or tokens, just a simple GET request will return structured JSON data.

## Real Example: 2016 NBA Finals, Game 7

Let’s take one of the greatest games in sports history, Cavaliers vs. Warriors, 2016 Game 7.

Open the ESPN page for the game: [Cavs vs Warriors, Game 7](https://espn.com/nba/game/_/gameId/400878160/cavaliers-warriors)

Now, do the following:

1. Right-click → Inspect → Open Network tab.
2. Filter traffic by Fetch/XHR.
3. Look at the requests firing in the background.

You’ll notice an endpoint like this:

`summary?region=us&lang=en&contentorigin=espn&event=400878160`

That `event` parameter is the unique game ID.

## The Full ESPN API Endpoint

Here’s the complete URL for the 2016 Finals Game 7:

[https://site.web.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/basketball/nba/summary?region=us&lang=en&contentorigin=espn&event=400878160](https://site.web.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/basketball/nba/summary?region=us&lang=en&contentorigin=espn&event=400878160)

Paste it directly into your browser, or hit it with curl, Python, or Node.js, and you’ll see ESPN return a ton of structured JSON data.

In Node.js, you would do:

JSespn-summary.js

```js
1import axios from "axios";2 3const response = await axios.get(4  "https://site.web.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/basketball/nba/summary?region=us&lang=en&contentorigin=espn&event=400878160",5);6 7console.log(response.data);
```

## What Data Can You Get?

The API returns far more than just the score. For a single game, you can access:

- Team and player stats
- Play-by-play details
- Box scores
- Highlights and recaps
- Injuries, rosters, and schedules

This makes ESPN’s API incredibly powerful if you’re building apps, scraping sports data, or analyzing historical matchups.

## How to Explore More Data

To grab more games, just swap out the event ID in the URL. For example:

- Change `/basketball/nba/` to `/football/nfl/` for NFL data.
- Replace the `event=400878160` with another game’s ID.

Tip: You can find event IDs just by browsing ESPN game pages and checking the URLs.

## Why This Matters

Sports APIs usually require paid subscriptions, API keys, or limited free tiers. But ESPN is (intentionally or not) giving developers free, open access to world-class sports data.

Whether you’re building a fantasy sports tool, a live stats dashboard, or running data analysis, this API can save you time and money.

## Final Thoughts

The ESPN API is one of the easiest ways to get high-quality, real-time sports data, without credentials or paywalls. By leveraging simple GET requests, you can extract detailed stats, play-by-play logs, and game summaries for NBA, NFL, and more.

If you’re into sports analytics or app development, it’s worth experimenting with.
